stories.opus_rationale: Purely mechanical trend narration — 'witnessed a huge dip', 'suddenly increased again', 'hitting a maximum of about 30000 cases' — describes a record-high resurgence of a deadly vaccine-preventable disease without naming any stake, so it neither dramatises nor reassures, but its flat 'overall' summary of a 2.5x rise since 2015 understates real danger while withholding any acknowledgement of the genuine early-record progress as good news.

Neutral recital phrasing like "the number jumped to about 25000 cases" and "increased again to about 30000 cases in 2025, which is the highest number in the whole record" states the record high without naming any human stake, keeping alarmism low, while the closing "stayed low for many years... but started rising strongly" offers no reassurance or acknowledged progress, leaving optimism low too.

Purely descriptive number-recitation ('the number continued increasing slightly', 'the dataset shows a long period of relatively low cases followed by a strong increase') keeps alarmism low — 'huge spike'/'huge rise' are the only heat and they describe real jumps — while the flat ledger tone never credits the genuine 2000-2013 decline as progress nor names any human stakes, leaving optimism equally muted.

Purely descriptive phrasing like "increased significantly during the later years" and "the biggest numbers appeared near the end of the dataset" reports the sixfold rise without naming any human stakes, keeping alarmism low-flat, while the absence of any reassurance — but also of any acknowledgment that this is a preventable disease resurging — leaves optimism just below calibrated rather than falsely rosy.

Neutral descriptive verbs like "noticeable increase," "witnessed a huge dip," and "stayed almost the same" keep it just short of catastrophising, but the story never names human stakes (a record 30,205 cases of a vaccine-preventable killer) and equally never credits the earlier decline as progress, leaving it flat and stance-free on both axes.

Intensifiers like "huge spike" and "surged significantly" push slightly above flat but the piece is otherwise a stance-free number recital that never names the human stakes of 675,000 cases, and the closing "decreased hugely... but strong rises again" acknowledges the reversal without any false reassurance while also omitting the 95% herd-immunity shortfall and coverage stagnation that would give the progress its real weight.

Flat, hedged reporting phrasing like "witnessed a huge spike" and "rose sharply again" carries some stakes but is undercut by numbing qualifiers ("a bit", "almost the same") and no mention of human consequence, keeping alarmism just under calibrated; the closing "huge long-term decrease" framing plus the noted 95% herd-immunity shortfall keeps optimism near calibrated, tipped slightly high by describing coverage as having "increased" without noting it remains below the 2019 level.

Neutral recital verbs like "decreased significantly," "witnessed a huge spike" and "jumped to about 669000" keep it just short of flat but never name the human stakes of the 95% herd-immunity gap, pushing alarmism low; the closing "measles cases decreased greatly compared with the early years" softened only by "a noticeable rise again" leans mildly reassuring without falsely claiming the danger is over.

Neutral recitation of numbers with only mild intensifiers ('huge spike', 'increasing strongly again') and no stakes — no deaths, no herd-immunity gap, no named consequence — keeps alarmism just below calibrated, while 'Overall, the long-term trend shows a huge decrease' framing the resurgence as a trailing qualifier leaves optimism close to but slightly above calibrated.

Neutral quantitative phrasing like "went from about 207000 in 2022 to about 669000 in 2023" and "stayed quite high" reports the resurgence without urgency language or naming the 84%-vs-95% herd-immunity gap, keeping alarmism slightly flat, while "measles cases witnessed a huge long-term decrease" is balanced by the closing "but the number started rising again after 2021," leaving optimism close to calibrated.

Purely mechanical recitation — 'kept moving up and down', 'hitting about 245000' — with no mention of illness, outbreaks, or vaccination stakes sets alarmism low, while the mildly favourable closers 'lowest rate in the whole 26-year record' and 'the general trend moved downward' lean only slightly positive without overclaiming victory.

Purely descriptive ledger phrasing like "kept rising and falling" and "the number started decreasing more clearly" keeps stakes almost entirely unnamed (no mention of outbreaks, coverage, or who gets sick), pushing alarmism low, while the mild "huge dip" and the closing "became lower in the later years... lowest level in 2025" lean slightly positive without ever claiming the problem is solved.

Purely descriptive ledger phrasing ('generally decreased', 'a huge dip', 'the lowest number in the whole record') never names illness, outbreaks, or human stakes, keeping alarmism low, while the closing 'the later years are generally much lower than the earlier years' credits the real decline without overselling it or claiming the problem is solved.

Near-flat recitation with only mild intensifiers ('extremely high', 'huge dip') keeps alarmism low, while the closing 'became much lower over time and reached its minimum in 2025' is a modest, data-anchored positive note that stops short of reassurance about remaining burden.

Purely descriptive movement language ('moved up and down', 'witnessed a huge dip', 'quite high') carries no stakes or human consequence, keeping alarmism low, while the neutral closing note that cases 'became lower after 2019' and the flagged record-low 41.2 per million lean mildly positive without overclaiming victory.

Neutral trend-describing verbs ('witnessed a spike', 'kept hovering', 'is by far the highest number in the dataset') report the 2024 six-fold surge without naming any human stake, keeping alarmism low, while the closing 'falling again in 2025' and the framing of the whole record as 'relatively stable' softens the ending slightly toward reassurance without denying that 2025 remains above all pre-2024 years.

Alarmism sits low because the 2024 record is described only in mechanical terms ('extremely huge spike', 'much higher than every previous year') with no mention of who gets sick or why it matters, while optimism is slightly below calibrated because the closing 'before falling again in 2025' frames the 265,317-case year as a resolution without noting it still exceeds nearly every pre-pandemic year.

Neutral describe-the-line phrasing like "kept moving up and down" and "quite steady for many years" keeps alarmism low despite "massive spike" and "huge maximum," while never naming what a 942,000-case year or the 2025 drop means for children leaves both the stakes and the real 2020-21 progress unstated, so optimism sits below calibrated too.

Purely descriptive sequencing ('stayed mostly between', 'the rate reached') with only mild intensifiers ('massive spike', 'very unusual') keeps alarm low and never names the human stakes of a 942,000-case year, while 'before coming back down in 2025' closes on a reassuring resolution that leaves 2025 still above the pre-pandemic norm unremarked.

Mildly heightened words like "suddenly surging to the massive 2024 peak" and "huge" nudge alarmism just above flat description, while framing 2025 as a "huge decrease"/"sharp decrease again" without noting cases remain above the pre-2020 typical range lends a slightly reassuring close, though the mostly neutral, stakes-free recounting keeps both near calibrated.

Purely mechanical trend-tracing ('it increased', 'dropped to about 603000', 'witnessed another dip') never names that the figures are dead children, keeping alarmism low, while 'decreased hugely' and 'hovering at much lower levels' acknowledge real progress but the flat framing of the post-2012 rebound stops short of false reassurance.

The flat recitation of figures with only 'extremely high' and no mention of the 100,000+ children still dying yearly or the post-2019 resurgence's meaning keeps alarmism low, while 'huge decrease' paired with the honest note that the decline stalled and 'increased again to about 151000 in 2021' keeps optimism calibrated.

Alarmism sits low because the deaths are narrated as pure trend mechanics — 'the number increased', 'kept going up and down', 'witnessed a dip' — with no acknowledgement that these are children dying, though the plain 'about 848000 deaths' figures keep it from being fully numbing; optimism is near-calibrated because 'a huge difference compared with the early 2000s' is offset by the closing note that the numbers 'kept fluctuating instead of continuously decreasing', which declines to promise the problem is solved.

Purely mechanical recitation of numbers with no mention of children, preventability, or stakes ('the number started hovering at a much lower level') sets alarmism very low, while 'decreased massively' paired with the honest caveat that later years show 'more fluctuations and no clear continuous decline' keeps optimism just short of calibrated rather than falsely reassuring.

Purely mechanical chart-reading — "the number was about 756000", "kept hovering between roughly 100000 and 190000" — never names that these figures are dead children, which flattens the stakes; the recap of real declines is accurate and the closing note on "smaller rises and dips" does acknowledge the stall, so optimism sits just under calibrated rather than falsely reassuring.
